title: Enter results
purpose: Enter awaiting results or new revisions of entered/returned work in a page-sized grid, then submit saved entries from the batch page.
summary: Enter results for the tests in this batch that are awaiting entry, entered or returned, a page at a time. Tests set up as calculated take readings. Saving does not submit anything for review.

tasks.title: Enter results
steps: Optionally set [[Default analysis start]] for every row that has no time of its own.
Type each result as read, a number or ND, and check its reporting limit and dilution.
Save the rows on this page. Submit them for review from the batch page.

tasks.title: Enter readings for a calculated test
steps: A row that says Calculated shows its readings with their units. Type each reading as read at the bench.
Check [[Reporting limit before dilution]] or [[Reporting limit in the solution]], and the [[Dilution]]. Where the row offers a weight basis in [[Soil basis]], keep it.
If the calculated value will fall below the reporting limit applied, add a qualifier or tick [[Report as ND]]. Then save the rows.

tasks.title: Enter a soil result corrected to dry weight
steps: On the row that says Calculated: Prepared solid corrected to dry weight, type the readings. Keep Dry weight in [[Soil basis]].
Under Percent solids for the dry-weight correction (required), type the sample's [[Percent solids]] and where it comes from in [[Solids source reference]].
Save the rows. The result and its reporting limit are worked out from the readings and that percent solids.

tasks.title: Correct a returned result
steps: Read the reviewer's reason under the row, enter the new result and give a [[Reason]], then save.

tasks.title: Record BOD5 bottle observations
steps: On a BOD5 row, select [[Record BOD5 bottles]].
Record and select complete bottle observations on that worksheet, then save. This row cannot take a final numeric result in the grid.

good_to_know: If any row has an error, nothing on the page is saved. Your typed values are kept so you can fix them.
A row you did not touch is skipped, even though the page filled in a reporting limit or offered a weight basis. A row you started, for example with a qualifier, must have its result.
A test set up as calculated takes readings, not a final result. If its calculation was added, removed or replaced after you opened the page, saving is refused and you reload.
Zero is a detected value; use ND for a non-detect. A value below its reporting limit needs a qualifier. For a calculated value, add one or tick [[Report as ND]].
Only this page is saved. Save before changing page, or what you typed is lost.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: These are staff pages. Active users with an application staff role can read them; client accounts cannot. Analysts perform result entry and batch work, reviewers decide results, and administrators maintain configuration. Administrators also have operational analyst and reviewer access, but independence rules still apply. Superuser status alone does not grant an application role.

items.label: Search
items.description: Partial, case-insensitive lab ID, client sample ID or analyte, across eligible current results in this batch.

items.label: Status
items.description: Defaults to All that need entry: awaiting, entered and returned. Choose Awaiting entry, Entered, not submitted or Returned. Submitted/approved results do not appear; use the result page or import for approved corrections.

items.label: Apply
items.description: Filter and return to page 1. Invalid filters produce errors and no rows.

items.label: Clear all
items.description: Restore the default enterable set.

items.label: Rows per page
items.description: 25 by default; choose 50 or 100. Paging preserves filters. Save before changing filters or page: unsaved entries are lost.

items.label: Default analysis start
items.description: Optional common laboratory-local start used only by rows without their own Analysis start.

items.label: Sample
items.description: Read-only laboratory sample ID.

items.label: Analyte
items.description: Read-only requested analyte.

items.label: Prepared aliquot
items.description: Explicit preparation choice; required where configured. Available choices are noncancelled aliquots linked to this requested test; the server validates their method and chronology.

items.label: Unit
items.description: Read-only test unit; no conversion.

items.label: Current
items.description: Latest supplied numeric value, or ND with its applied reporting-limit threshold, and current status; a value worked from readings is marked calculated. New fields are not populated from it.

items.label: Soil basis
items.description: For soil only, choose Wet weight or Dry weight. Not applicable is shown among choices but is rejected for a new soil observation. On a row of a calculated test whose calculation means one basis, the row offers it: Dry weight for a prepared solid corrected to dry weight, Wet weight for percent solids and percent moisture. Any other basis is refused when you save, with what you typed kept. The prepared solid as weighed and the other calculations offer no basis: you declare wet or dry weight.

items.label: Supplied percent solids (optional)
items.description: Expand Percent solids and Solids source reference for soil. On a row whose calculation corrects to dry weight the heading reads Percent solids for the dry-weight correction (required), and the details open by themselves.

items.label: Percent solids
items.description: Optional supplied exact percentage beside a typed result; requires a source. For a calculation corrected to dry weight it is required, must be greater than zero and at most 100, and is the value the correction is worked with. It is kept on the worksheet as a reading. It is typed here, once: the calculation has no reading box for it, and it is not taken from the sample's percent solids result.

items.label: Solids source reference
items.description: Required with supplied solids, at most 240 characters; identifies the actual measurement/source. Always required with a calculation corrected to dry weight.

items.label: Result
items.description: Number or ND as observed, for a test that takes a typed result. To skip a row, leave it untouched. The reporting limit and the dilution of 1 that the page filled in, and the weight basis the page offered, do not count as typed. Anything else typed or chosen in the row (a changed limit or dilution, qualifiers, a reason, an analysis start, a prepared aliquot, other soil details) makes it an entry, and an entry with no result is an error (Result is required).

items.label: Result or readings
items.description: The column heading when any row on the page is calculated. A row of a calculated test shows Calculated: followed by the calculation and its version, one box for each reading with its unit, and Report as ND, instead of the Result box. Other rows keep the Result box.

items.label: Readings
items.description: Typed as read, exactly, with no rounding. Each must be a number (an instrument reading may be ND). Weights cannot be negative, and volumes, the reporting limit and the weight of a prepared solid must be greater than zero. Dilution calculation: Instrument reading in the unit of the test and Reporting limit before dilution, offered from the catalog limit. Solids by weight: Dried residue with its filter or dish and Filter or dish alone (g or mg, matching the calculation) and Sample volume (mL). Preparation by volume: Instrument reading, Reporting limit in the solution, Sample volume prepared (mL) and Final volume (mL). Prepared solid as weighed or corrected to dry weight: Instrument reading, Reporting limit in the solution, Final volume (mL) and Sample weight (g), called Sample weight as received for the dry-weight correction. Percent solids and percent moisture by weight: Dish alone, Dish with the sample as received and Dish with the dried sample (g); the dried sample cannot weigh less than the dish or more than the sample as received. The limit in the solution is typed with each result for the preparation calculations; it is not filled in. A row with more than three readings lays them out two to a line.

items.label: Report as ND
items.description: Only on rows of a calculated test. Tick it to report a calculated value as ND when the value is below the reporting limit applied; it is refused when the value is not below the limit. The readings and the calculated value stay on record either way.

items.label: Reporting limit
items.description: Applied limit for this observation. Initially the current method limit if configured; check and edit as needed. With browser scripting, entering a positive whole-number dilution multiplies that base limit until you manually edit the limit. Fractional dilution does not auto-calculate it. For the dilution calculation the cell shows Calculated: limit before dilution × dilution instead of a box. For the preparation calculations (by volume, prepared solid) it shows Calculated: limit in the solution × the same factors, rounded like the result: the limit is worked out from Reporting limit in the solution and the other readings, then rounded by the test's rounding rule. For solids by weight, percent solids and percent moisture the limit is still typed.

items.label: Dilution
items.description: Initially 1. Record the actual positive factor. The dilution, preparation by volume and prepared solid calculations multiply by it. For solids by weight, percent solids and percent moisture the cell shows Not used: no dilution factor is applied and it is saved as 1.

items.label: Qualifiers
items.description: Optional active, case-sensitive codes separated by commas, semicolons or whitespace. Duplicates are removed; unknown/inactive codes are errors.

items.label: Analysis start
items.description: Required per entered row unless Default analysis start is supplied. Row value overrides the default.

items.label: Reason
items.description: Shown for a result that already has a revision. Required for correction of returned/approved work; a draft revision without a reason receives the recorded reason Entry revised before submission.

items.label: How to enter results
items.description: Collapsed above the grid: how to type results (exact text, ND for a non-detect), the reporting-limit default, units and time zone, and the active qualifier codes with descriptions. Codes marked for holding-time exceedance can satisfy the exceeded-time submission requirement. On a soil batch the weight-basis rule stays visible above it, and, when a row is calculated, a note says the row offers the basis its calculation means and that a result corrected to dry weight needs the sample's percent solids and its source.

items.label: Returned row
items.description: A result returned by review shows a Returned line under its row with the reviewer's reason and name. Enter it again with a reason.

sections.title: Exact results and chronology
paragraphs: Use a plain decimal number, optionally signed or in scientific notation, or ND (case-insensitive) for a non-detect. Zero is a detected numeric observation, never an inferred non-detect. Comparison symbols, units, thousands separators and values needing rounding are rejected. Result text is limited to 60 characters; numeric observations support 14 integer digits and 10 decimal places.

Reporting limit must be positive. Dilution must be positive with at most four decimal places and at most ten integer digits. A detected value below its applied reporting limit needs at least one active qualifier or must be entered as ND where appropriate; the application does not choose that interpretation for you. Units come from the test; nothing is converted.

Analysis cannot precede sample receipt or applicable preparation, and cannot be more than two minutes ahead of the current time. Preparation cannot precede collection, including composite end. Local form times use the deployment’s laboratory time zone; ambiguous/nonexistent daylight-saving local times are rejected.

For soil, choose Wet weight or Dry weight for every new observation. For a typed result, enter the final result and reporting limit on that same basis; no conversion is performed. Percent solids is optional exact supplied data between 0 and 100 inclusive, and requires its source reference, unless a dry-weight calculation needs it (then it is required and must be greater than zero). A reference without percent solids is invalid. Nonsoil results use Not applicable and reject supplied solids metadata.

An active independent preparation requirement needs an explicit available aliquot for this sample/test, matrix and required preparation method/version. It must have a recorded start, and analysis cannot precede completion when recorded, otherwise start. Choosing the same aliquot means repeat analysis; choosing a new physical aliquot means re-preparation. No identity is inferred from a legacy batch timestamp.

sections.title: Calculated rows
paragraphs: An administrator can set a calculation rule for a test under QC configuration. For that test, manual entry takes readings and a typed final result is refused. File imports are unchanged: they supply final values, get no worksheet and are not recalculated. QC sample measurements are still typed.

Calculations available: Reading times dilution factor (result = instrument reading × dilution factor; reporting limit applied = limit before dilution × dilution factor; a reading of ND gives ND at that limit). Solids by weight with the balance in grams or milligrams (mg/L = (dried residue with its filter or dish − filter or dish alone) × 1,000,000 ÷ mL for grams, × 1,000 for milligrams); these apply no dilution factor and no blank correction. Preparation by volume (result = instrument reading × final volume ÷ sample volume prepared × dilution factor). Prepared solid as weighed, in three unit pairings (mg/L in solution to mg/kg, ug/L to ug/kg, ug/L to mg/kg): result = instrument reading × final volume in mL ÷ sample weight in g × dilution factor, divided by 1,000 again for ug/L to mg/kg. It applies no percent solids correction: the result is on the basis of the portion as weighed, and you declare wet or dry weight. Prepared solid corrected to dry weight, in the same three pairings, for soil tests only: the same arithmetic divided by percent solids ÷ 100. Percent solids by weight and percent moisture by weight, in %: three weights in g (dish alone, dish with the sample as received, dish with the dried sample); on a soil entry you must declare Wet weight, and the reporting limit is typed.

The preparation calculations work out the reporting limit applied themselves: the limit in the solution times the same factors as the result, then rounded by the test's rounding rule, the same rule as the result. A reading of ND gives ND at that limit. A rounding that takes the limit to zero is refused when you save.

The value is carried at full precision and rounded once, at the end, by the laboratory's rule for that test. A calculated value below the reporting limit applied needs a qualifier to be reported, or Report as ND. Saving keeps a worksheet with the revision: the calculation and version, every reading as typed (including the percent solids a dry-weight result was worked with), the value before rounding, the reporting limit before rounding where the calculation works it out, and the rounding applied. The result page shows it.

What the calculations do not do: the percent solids for the dry-weight correction is typed with its source and is not taken from the sample's percent solids result. Preparation amounts (volumes and weights) are typed with each result; they are not recorded once on a prepared aliquot. One calculation applies to a test, so a test is either corrected to dry weight or not.

items.label: Save … rows on this page as entered
items.description: Analysts save attempted rows on this page only. Every saved observation becomes a new entered revision and retains previous entries; it does not submit for review. A save with no attempted entries produces an error.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Return to the batch without saving typed values.

items.label: Row errors
items.description: If any submitted row is invalid, nothing in this save is committed. Errors link to affected rows and preserve typed values. A row is skipped only when nothing is typed or chosen in it; a row that was started but has no result or readings is an error, never dropped. Reading errors appear beside the reading; a calculated row reports every problem it has together.

items.label: Changed rows
items.description: If a submitted result is no longer an eligible current result of this batch, nothing is saved. Reload, check current rows and enter again; do not assume unsaved values survive reload. The same applies when a calculation rule was added or deactivated, or its calculation replaced, after you opened the page: saving is refused with the reason, and you reload. A change to the rounding alone applies from your next save.

items.label: Preparation time needed
items.description: Resolve the linked missing preparation start before entry; a result entered without a required clock event cannot be submitted until re-entered with the correct event.

sections.title: Empty states
paragraphs: Clear filters if no rows match. Nothing to enter can mean no tests or all tests are submitted/approved. Add tests from the batch where appropriate. Returned rows are supported by this grid and the result page. Other staff can inspect the disabled entry form but cannot save it.

sections.title: Titration readings and limits
paragraphs: Alkalinity by titration to pH 4.5, Low alkalinity by two-endpoint titration and Total hardness by EDTA titration produce mg/L as CaCO3. The test must use that exact unit and cannot be soil. The laboratory chooses the calculation per test; a result never switches the procedure automatically.

Use one uninterrupted burette run. Readings cannot be negative or go backward; a refill is not inferred. The low-alkalinity final burette reading must exceed the first endpoint reading. The single-endpoint equations permit equal initial and final readings.

These worksheets apply no dilution factor (saved as 1), preparation factor or blank correction. Enter the reporting limit that applies to the result; it is not scaled. Readings must be numbers, not ND. A calculated value below the limit needs a qualifier or Report as ND, with the readings and calculated value retained. A negative low-alkalinity value is not changed to zero.

The sources are historical EPA method equations, not a statement of current regulatory approval. The pH 3.9 mineral-acid procedure and the separate low-hardness blank procedure are not included. The laboratory checks titrant standardization, endpoint suitability and method acceptance. Low alkalinity describes below 20 mg/L and a 100–200 mL portion in its source; the application does not determine that suitability or enforce those bounds.

items.label: Initial burette reading
items.description: Required mL reading before adding titrant. It is subtracted from each endpoint reading, so the burette need not start at zero.

items.label: Final burette reading
items.description: Required mL reading at the final endpoint, on the same burette run. For alkalinity to pH 4.5 and hardness, titrant volume is final minus initial. For low alkalinity it gives C, the total volume from the initial reading, not the additional volume after the first endpoint.

items.label: First endpoint burette reading
items.description: Low alkalinity only. Required mL reading at the first endpoint. B is this reading minus the initial reading; the equation uses 2B minus C, not B minus C.

items.label: Sample volume
items.description: Required positive mL of original sample aliquot titrated. For either alkalinity worksheet use an unaltered sample, with no added dilution water. For hardness exclude reagents and water added in the titration vessel from the original aliquot volume. No separate preparation dilution correction is applied.

items.label: Standardized acid normality
items.description: Alkalinity only. Required positive actual standardized acid strength in N (equivalents per liter). No nominal strength is assumed.

items.label: Standardized EDTA normality
items.description: Hardness only. Required positive actual standardized EDTA strength in N (equivalents per liter), not molarity or mg CaCO3 per mL. No nominal strength is assumed.

items.label: Endpoint pH
items.description: Alkalinity to pH 4.5 only. Required measured endpoint pH, exactly 4.5 for this equation; 4.50 is equivalent. Another endpoint is refused with the entered readings kept. No acceptance tolerance is inferred.

items.label: First endpoint pH
items.description: Low alkalinity only. Required measured first endpoint pH, from 4.3 through 4.7 inclusive.

items.label: Final endpoint pH
items.description: Low alkalinity only. Required measured pH after further acid addition, exactly 0.3 below the first endpoint pH. A different pair is refused with the readings kept; no tolerance or interpolation is applied.

sections.title: BOD5 bottle entry
paragraphs: Each bottle value in mg/L is (initial DO − final DO − entered seed correction) × filled bottle volume ÷ sample volume. The arithmetic mean gives each included bottle equal weight, even when volumes differ. The common prior dilution factor multiplies that mean once, and only that final result is rounded by the test rule. Excluded bottles never contribute to the mean.

A BOD5 test row shows its analyte, unit and BOD5 bottle worksheet instead of numeric entry fields. Analysts follow Record BOD5 bottles to its dedicated page. Other staff can inspect the batch grid but are not offered the entry link. Saving this grid does not save bottle observations; entering a final numeric value for a BOD5 row is refused.

The separate worksheet keeps 1–12 complete rows, original strings, per-bottle correction sources and explicit Include/Exclude choices. Excluded rows require reasons and at least one bottle must be included. Add/Remove only changes current entry rows; saving creates a revision and retains earlier ones.

This is BOD5 arithmetic only. It does not estimate seed demand from controls, subtract dilution-water blank demand, assess incubation or method eligibility, apply automatic bottle QC thresholds, or establish regulatory approval. CBOD5 is outside its scope. The analyst assesses the laboratory method and QC before selection; Include is not an automatic acceptance verdict.

items.label: Record BOD5 bottles
items.description: Open the dedicated worksheet for this test. A current batch assignment and analyst access are required; a submitted result must be returned before editing. Entry errors keep input, and a stale revision or replaced calculation requires reload.

sections.title: Recorded calibration evidence
paragraphs: A calibration link is optional. It points to the recorded instrument evidence. The calibration record’s Calibration fit worksheet is for inspection only. Follow the laboratory’s procedure for method acceptance, source independence, sequencing and bracketing.

items.label: Calibration
items.description: Optional immutable instrument-reported curve for the result’s current batch, test and unit. In the single-result Enter result or Correct result form, choose it explicitly for every revision. Blank means Not linked and never carries an earlier link forward. The curve’s recorded time must precede or coincide with analysis.

items.label: Calibration verification
items.description: Optional current calibration-verification QC observation for the same batch, test and unit, used only with a selected curve. The observation must be at or after calibration; a closing check may follow sample analysis. Its label, exact observed text, true value, unit, time and identity are frozen with the revision.

items.label: Correction and independence
items.description: If a selected QC observation is superseded, submission, approval and release are held until a new result revision records current evidence. People who recorded the selected curve or check cannot independently review or release that result. Existing QC, holding-time and preservation gates still apply.

items.label: Where links are entered
items.description: Only the single-result form offers evidence choices. Grid entry, CSV/TSV/XLSX import and BOD5 bottle entry do not infer or carry calibration links. A later correction using those paths also leaves the new revision unlinked.

items.label: Stale form
items.description: If a result changed after the single-result form was opened, saving is refused and the input is kept. Reload to inspect the current revision before entering a correction.
